title: "Prerequisites"
---

::: {.ao-story}
Before the road, the quartermaster checks your pack. A traveller without a lantern turns back at the first tunnel. Check each item when a lesson asks for it, and install your agent only when you reach Set Up Your Agent.
:::

This page lists what to install for the hands-on exercises. Reading is separate: see [Read first](read-first.html). Nothing here needs real data. Exercises use invented files unless the page says otherwise.

## Required

| Tool | Check it works | Needed for |
|---|---|---|
| A terminal | open it and type `echo hello` | every exercise |
| Python 3 | `python3 --version` | the exercises that run a small Python script, such as Ground Truth |
| git | `git --version` | the undo and change-history exercises |

- **Terminal.** macOS: Terminal. Linux: any terminal. Windows: a WSL 2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux) terminal, because the exercises assume a Linux-style shell and the sandbox needs it. Follow Microsoft's WSL install page, then open the Ubuntu terminal.

## Pick a route for the agent

An agent is a model with tools that can read your files and run commands. You do not need one yet. [Set Up Your Agent](zones/agents-and-models/set-up-your-agent.html) gives the full install steps and the first session for each route, and the tabs on every lesson follow the route you pick there. The two routes are Claude Code, which uses a hosted model, and OpenCode with Ollama, which runs a model on your own computer.

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

| Tool | Check it works |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude --version` |

- **Install.** Set Up Your Agent gives the installer command. Read an installer script before piping it into `bash` (piping sends the downloaded script straight to the shell to run). To read it first, download it with `curl -fsSL <url> | less`.
- **An account.** Claude Code needs a login on a paid Claude plan, or an Anthropic API key (a secret string that gives programmatic access, billed per use). Use the account your organisation approves.

## OpenCode + Ollama

| Tool | Check it works |
|---|---|
| Ollama (runs a model on your own computer) | `ollama --version` |
| OpenCode (an open-source coding agent) | `opencode --version` |

- **Install.** Set Up Your Agent gives the Ollama and OpenCode install commands and the model to fetch.
- **No account.** Prompts stay on your computer. You need about 16 GB of memory and 5 GB of free disk. A small local model holds less in mind and makes more mistakes than a hosted one, so check its answers.

:::

## Optional

| Tool | Check it works | Needed for |
|---|---|---|
| bubblewrap and socat | `bwrap --version` | the sandbox exercise on Linux and WSL 2 (two helper tools). A sandbox is an operating-system boundary that limits what a command can touch |
| Docker | `docker --version` | the boundary exercise on the OpenCode route (a container is an isolated Linux environment; Docker Desktop must be running). Skip it if your machine does not allow it |

Using an LLM is always your choice. The lessons show what to check if you do.

## A first check

Run this once from any folder. Each tool should print a version number. Then run the version command for your agent route:

```bash
python3 --version && git --version
```

## If something fails

- `command not found`: the program is not installed, or its folder is not on your `PATH` (the list of folders the shell searches for programs).
- If the shell cannot find `claude`, add its folder to `PATH`: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` in `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`, then open a new terminal. If it cannot find `opencode` or `ollama`, open a new terminal and try again.
- On a managed laptop, ask your administrator before installing.
- Do not run the exercises on a cluster login node (the shared machine you log in to first).
